key_insight: This paper reframes computer vision as a unified multimodal generation problem, where different vision tasks can be handled by the same model through text and image generation. Instead of building task-specific heads or architectures, one model can output text, images, or mixed outputs depending on the instruction.
problem_solved: It addresses the fragmentation of computer vision systems, where each task often needs its own specialized architecture, decoding strategy, or output format. The paper aims to make vision models more flexible, general, and easier to extend across heterogeneous tasks.
method: Uses a unified multimodal model, SenseNova-Vision, to express vision tasks in native text and image generation spaces.
Accepts natural-language instructions plus optional visual prompts to specify the task, target region, view, or decoding convention.
Generates different output types depending on the task: text for symbolic results, images for dense spatial predictions, or mixed outputs when needed.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this approach reduces the need for task-specific engineering and makes it easier to deploy one model across many vision applications. It also opens the door to more scalable, instruction-driven vision systems that can adapt to new tasks with less redesign.
